modes.cue_notes: From Shoelace (stacked knees), hinge forward from the hips and walk the hands forward. Allow the spine to round into the forward fold. The outer hip of both legs receives a compounded stretch. If the hips are uneven (one side higher than the other), use a block under the elevated hip. Hold each side (switching top and bottom knee).

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: An intensification of Shoelace (Gomukhasana legs) by adding a forward fold over the stacked knees. The gallbladder meridian along the outer hip and IT band receives maximum compressive and tensile stress.

breathing_cues.entering: From Shoelace, inhale to find length in the spine. On a slow, complete exhale, walk the hands forward and allow the torso to drape over the stacked knees, rounding the entire spine.
breathing_cues.holding: Breathe into the back of the outer hips. Each exhale invites the gallbladder meridian line, lateral hip, IT band, outer knee, to release incrementally. Soften the jaw, throat, and hands completely.
breathing_cues.exiting: On an inhale, press the palms into the floor and slowly unwind the spine to upright. Release the legs and take a brief rebound in constructive rest before switching sides.

modifications.name: Stay Upright
modifications.description: Remain in Shoelace without adding the forward fold. This is the prop-free variation and appropriate when the outer hip is already at capacity.

modifications.name: Bolster in Front
modifications.description: Place a bolster lengthwise in front of the stacked knees and rest the torso on it, allowing the forward fold to be fully passive without any muscular effort.

modifications.name: Hands on Floor Beside Shins
modifications.description: Keep the hands on the floor on either side of the shins rather than walking them forward, maintaining a slight upright hinge rather than a full forward fold.

emotional_release_potential.notes: Maximum compressive load on the gallbladder meridian territory (outer hip, IT band) in this pose can surface deeply stored frustration or unresolved anger.
The combination of compression and forward fold asks the body to completely yield, a direct confrontation with the psychological tendency to hold on and resist release.
